findings.category: OWASP A07 Identification and Authentication Failures
findings.title: Child can claim parent ownership during first pairing
findings.description: The child-visible pairing code is sufficient to choose the first parent password.
findings.exploit_scenario: The child opens the local cabinet, copies the code shown on the same PC, submits setup first, and becomes the configured parent.
findings.impact: Full control over approvals, maintenance mode, PIN, app policy and account actions.
findings.recommendation: Require an already authenticated parent passkey session to claim a device public key; make enrollment single-use and rate-limited.
findings.playbook: Do not deploy the current first-pairing flow on a child-controlled PC.

findings.category: OWASP A07 Identification and Authentication Failures
findings.title: Known default PIN can disable or uninstall protection
findings.description: An empty PIN becomes 123456, including after pairing because setup does not replace it.
findings.exploit_scenario: The child selects Disable Guard or starts uninstall and enters the public default PIN.
findings.impact: All Guard enforcement is removed or paused.
findings.recommendation: Remove child-side reusable PIN bypasses; authorize maintenance from the parent device and use a high-entropy offline recovery package.
findings.playbook: Treat every installation with an unset PIN as unprotected.

findings.title: Privileged enforcement is an interactive per-user process
findings.description: Guard requires admin rights but relies on HKCU and an interactive ONLOGON task tied to the installer identity.
findings.exploit_scenario: The child uses a separate standard account where the parent task is absent, or targets the user-session process and helper.
findings.impact: Enforcement can fail to start, cannot reliably observe the child session, and has weak tamper resistance.
findings.recommendation: Move enforcement and state to a LocalSystem Windows service; use a separate child-session UI over ACL-restricted named pipes.
findings.playbook: Do not claim standard-user protection until reboot/logon behavior is validated in a VM.
findings.verification: self-verified by installer, manifest and startup-task source trace

findings.title: Web default-deny is browser-UI dependent and bypassable
findings.description: Only a short browser process list is inspected with UI Automation after a page is foregrounded.
findings.exploit_scenario: Use an unsupported or portable browser, raw IP, DoH, VPN/proxy, background request, or a browser state where the address bar is not exposed.
findings.impact: Unapproved web access succeeds or is not attributed correctly.
findings.recommendation: Manage approved browsers with forced policy/extension and add network egress controls; block every unmanaged browser and tunnel app.
findings.playbook: Treat the current browser feature as best-effort telemetry, not enforcement.

findings.title: AppLocker baseline leaves documented bypass hosts available
findings.description: The policy keeps Windows allow rules and blocks only a partial hand-written tool list; packaged apps and DLLs are not covered.
findings.exploit_scenario: Invoke a Microsoft-signed script or application-control bypass host that remains allowed, or install/run a permitted packaged app.
findings.impact: Arbitrary code or prohibited applications can run under the child account.
findings.recommendation: Build a versioned least-privilege policy from Microsoft bypass guidance and evaluate signed App Control for Business for secure mode.
findings.playbook: Keep enforcement in audit mode until the complete policy is validated on the target Windows build.
findings.verification: self-verified against Microsoft AppLocker security guidance

findings.title: Parent cabinet transmits credentials and sessions over LAN HTTP
findings.description: The listener binds to http://+ and has no TLS, login/setup throttling, CSRF token, request-size limit or trusted host validation.
findings.exploit_scenario: A LAN peer observes or attacks parent traffic, brute-forces login/setup, or exhausts the listener with oversized forms.
findings.impact: Parent session theft, policy changes, privacy exposure or denial of service.
findings.recommendation: Replace LAN password auth with an outbound TLS device channel and passkey-protected parent controller; harden any temporary local endpoint.
findings.playbook: Do not expose the current listener on untrusted networks.

findings.category: OWASP A08 Software and Data Integrity Failures
findings.title: Policy state is non-atomic, same-user scoped and replayable
findings.description: Direct writes to three CurrentUser-DPAPI files swallow errors and have no monotonic anti-rollback control.
findings.exploit_scenario: A same-user process deletes, corrupts or restores an older protected state while concurrent server and timer writes race.
findings.impact: Crash, rollback to weaker rules, lost approvals or inconsistent enforcement.
findings.recommendation: Let the service exclusively own ProgramData state with SYSTEM/admin ACLs, atomic replace, versioning and rollback detection.
findings.playbook: Preserve current files for migration but never trust their newest/oldest copy without validation.

findings.title: Installer and executables are unsigned and no CI release gate exists
findings.description: Authenticode status is NotSigned for the installer and all executable components; no workflow builds or verifies releases.
findings.exploit_scenario: A modified installer/helper is substituted or a broken policy build is shipped without reproducible verification.
findings.impact: Supply-chain compromise, tamper bypass or widespread lockout.
findings.recommendation: Sign every artifact and update manifest; add reproducible CI, VM acceptance gates, staged rollout and rollback verification.
findings.playbook: Do not distribute the current installer as a trusted security product.
findings.verification: self-verified with Get-AuthenticodeSignature and repository inspection

findings.category: OWASP A07 Identification and Authentication Failures
findings.title: Windows parent-account recovery bypass is not prevented
findings.description: Setup can demote the child but does not require an offline local parent admin or continuously enforce account/group invariants.
findings.exploit_scenario: The child resets the parent Microsoft-account PIN/password through email access, signs in as administrator, and changes Guard or Windows policy.
findings.impact: Full local administrator compromise and complete bypass.
findings.recommendation: Require a separate local parent admin without email reset on the child PC, standard child account, admin-group monitoring, BitLocker and controlled recovery keys.
findings.playbook: Remove the parent's Microsoft account from the child PC before any live Guard test.
findings.verification: self-verified against current source and Microsoft PIN-reset behavior

findings.title: Internet parent approval is not implemented
findings.description: The current parent cabinet is LAN-only.
findings.exploit_scenario: The parent is away from home and never receives or cannot act on a request.
findings.impact: The primary product workflow fails outside the local network.
findings.recommendation: Add an outbound-only TLS device connection to a cloud relay and a passkey-protected parent PWA with secret-free push notifications.
findings.playbook: Document current operation as LAN-only until the secure relay exists.

findings.title: Parent workflow is settings-first rather than request-first
findings.description: A single long page mixes requests, blocklists, paths, PIN, accounts, limits and maintenance.
findings.exploit_scenario: A tired parent enters the wrong executable path, grants forever by mistake, or disables protection to complete a simple task.
findings.impact: Misconfiguration becomes the easiest practical bypass.
findings.recommendation: Make requests the home screen, use scoped approval presets, and move advanced controls behind persistent navigation and explicit safety states.
findings.playbook: Do not add more controls to the existing single-page dashboard.
findings.verification: self-verified by source-based UX review; visual screenshot audit pending VM run

findings.title: Russian and English localization is incomplete
findings.description: Localization is embedded ad hoc; pairing is mostly Russian while cleaner and installer remain English-only.
findings.exploit_scenario: A parent misunderstands a destructive or recovery action in an inconsistent language.
findings.impact: Setup errors, unsafe recovery and reduced trust.
findings.recommendation: Use resource-based RU/EN localization for installer, service errors, child UI, recovery and parent UI, with Russian default and localization tests.
findings.playbook: Treat technical logs as separate from user-facing localized text.

findings.title: Security-critical Windows behavior has no VM end-to-end coverage
findings.description: All 35 pure-logic checks pass, but installer, service startup, browser bypasses, account changes, reboot and recovery are untested.
findings.exploit_scenario: A release passes unit tests while protection silently fails after logon, update, browser change or reboot.
findings.recommendation: Create a Windows 11 24H2/25H2 VM matrix with scripted attack cases and release-blocking acceptance gates.
findings.playbook: Do not run system enforcement tests on Ivan's daily machine.
